messages:
Maya (CSM): quick heads-up — Halcyon Health onboarding hit a tail-latency spike this morning after ramp: p95 jumped to ~1.4s and token spend up ~35% week over week. customer is nervous about perf for renewal signal. can we propose a minimal-risk mitigation? :warning:
Oliver (Solutions): thanks. do we have traces or a route breakdown? is this concentrated on specific endpoints or models?
Maya (CSM): most of it is on /v1/chat (triage) — their traffic pattern has longer contexts and lots of short-turn chats. I attached the console snapshot in the onboarding doc but pasting quick stats: p50 240ms, p95 1.4s, error rate stable.
perfbot: [metric alert] halcyon.health /v1/chat — p95 increased 2.8x since yesterday, token cost rate +33%. Top models: redwood-xxlarge-v1 (75%), redwood-large-v1 (20%), misc smalls 5%.
Sam (SRE): looks like tail is model-bound. quick win is moving some traffic to a quantized variant for cost + tail improvements while keeping fallback. propose canary 10% -> 30% after 2h if p95 improves.
Devon (ML Eng): agree. recommend `redwood-large-q4_0` for this workload — preserves logits but reduces per-token compute. Expect ~25-40% cost drop and better GPU throughput. There is a slight quality delta on very long contexts; we should include a small eval set from their prod prompts.
Oliver (Solutions): propose routing change: add a routing rule by route key and content-length heuristic. short/medium contexts -> quantized variant; long contexts -> xxlarge with KV cache pin. fallback to xxlarge on regen errors. sample config (canary):
```
route: /v1/chat
rules:
  - condition: tokens <= 1024
    model: redwood-large-q4_0
    percent: 10
  - condition: tokens > 1024
    model: redwood-xxlarge-v1
    percent: 90
fallbacks:
  - model: redwood-xxlarge-v1
```
Maya (CSM): perfect. I'll ask Halcyon for a small prompt corpus for evaluation and align on quality thresholds. they care most about hallucination frequency and factuality on patient-facing content.
Devon (ML Eng): please capture ~200 representative prompts. we can run automated evals (BLEU/ROUGE + custom QA checks) and human spot-check 20 examples. if delta < 2% on our QA metric we can widen canary.
Sam (SRE): ops checklist before canary:
• Create canary route with traffic shadowing enabled
• Set p95 SLO alert at +30% over baseline
• Auto rollback if error rate > 0.5% or hallucination regression flagged by eval pipeline
Oliver (Solutions): I'll own rollout and monitor. timeline: request prompt corpus by EOD Wed, run eval Thu, canary Fri if all green.
Maya (CSM): looping in customer for corpus ask. also logging this as a renewal-risk mitigation play in the account (Halcyon Health) — will include notes in the renewal tracker.
perfbot: [note] created ticket CS-4221 for canary rollout runbook.
Maya (CSM): any other quick low-friction wins?
Devon (ML Eng): recommend small changes in prefix-caching settings for /v1/chat — their bot uses a lot of repeated system prompts. enable prefix cache (TTL 10m) could shave ~10-15% tail.
Sam (SRE): agree. that's low-risk, I'll toggle in staging and report numbers.
Oliver (Solutions): summary action items:
1) Maya: collect 200 prompts from Halcyon (due EOD Wed)
2) Devon: run evals and human spot-check (Thu)
3) Sam: stage prefix cache + create canary route with alerts (Thu-Fri)
4) Oliver: execute canary at 10% and monitor, expand if p95 improves and eval passes
Maya (CSM): thanks team — I'll update customer and put a short note in the renewal tracker. ping me if you want me to nudge the customer on prioritizing the corpus. :thumbsup:
Oliver (Solutions): thanks — will post canary status updates in this thread.
Maya (CSM): (added) customer asked if there will be visible change to latency for end users immediately — i'll tell them small improvement expected for most flows, major gains once we widen canary.
Devon (ML Eng): +1. also capture any qualitative feedback they send during canary (e.g., fluency differences) so we can surface to model team.
Maya (CSM): will do. closing loop later with results. :handshake:
